scope: Family 120 almost-linear matching / prescribed-degree factor algorithm interpreted as constrained molecular interaction-graph design. Earlier N50 certificate-search finding retained only as a scoped negative note.
overall_status: Family-120 theorem is source-reported, not independently verified. Molecular mapping and toy energetic obstruction are internally reconstructed and precisely scoped; no real-world chemistry claim is established.

claims.exact_statement: For a supplied simple undirected graph G=([n],E), m=|E|, p=n+m, adjacency-list representation, and one-word integers f(v) satisfying 0<=f(v)<=deg_G(v), define an f-factor as F subseteq E with deg_F(v)=f(v) for every v. The pinned family-120 manuscript states that one uniform randomized word-RAM algorithm halts on every computation path within C_f p^(1+eta_f(p)) instructions, where eta_f(p)->0; outputs either an explicitly validated f-factor or NO; returns an f-factor with probability at least 2/3 if one exists; and always returns NO if none exists.
assumptions: G is explicit, simple, finite, undirected, and supplied as adjacency lists.
The target-degree array is supplied and satisfies the source's one-word and local-range conditions.
The source theorem and matching subroutine are correct as stated; this worker did not independently verify their proof.
claims.status: SOURCE_REPORTED; theorem statement/interface extracted, proof not independently audited or implemented.
claims.novelty_boundary: The source claims an almost-linear graph algorithm. The f-factor problem and polynomial-time algorithms are classical. This report makes no independent priority, correctness, or novelty claim about the release theorem.
costs: Source-claimed total worst-case instruction bound is C_f p^(1+eta_f(p)) on every random path.

The one-word f array, O(n+m log(n+2)) reduction, O(m log(n+2))-size matching instance, matching computation, witness checks, decoding, random bits, and output are within the source's word-RAM accounting.
Candidate edge acquisition, molecular parameter estimation, force-field computation, and experiments are not part of the formal input or cost bound.
claims.falsifier: A counterexample to the source theorem's claimed algorithmic guarantee under the stated finite simple-graph and word-RAM interface, or a gap in its proof/reduction that invalidates its guarantee.
claims.next_gate: Independent proof audit or a faithful executable implementation with adversarial and exhaustive small-instance checks; finite tests alone would not prove the asymptotic theorem.

claims.exact_statement: A constrained topology-design instance can be represented by a simple candidate-contact graph G=(V,E), where each edge is one permitted unit contact, and integer f(v) is the exact number of selected new contacts required at site v. Any returned f-factor is an exact graph-feasibility witness. Under the family-120 source guarantee, no-factor inputs always receive NO, while feasible inputs receive a valid witness with probability at least 2/3; thus NO on a feasible input is possible and is not an infeasibility certificate.
assumptions: One permitted contact per unordered site pair; no edge multiplicity or edge weight is required.
All chemical legality constraints relevant to the modeled decision are fully represented by this simple graph and exact degree targets, or have a separately proved encoding.
The family-120 theorem is true as source-reported.
claims.status: INTERNALLY_RECONSTRUCTED APPLICATION INTERFACE, CONDITIONAL ON RRL-F120-C1; no experimental or general molecular-design result.
claims.proof_path: work/agents/reaction_recognition_logic/FINAL_REPORT.md#molecular-interface-and-scope; one-sided error follows directly from Corollary 10.1 text in family120.txt:3920-3979.
claims.novelty_boundary: This is a formal problem translation, not a claim that real chemistry naturally reduces to an unweighted f-factor. It certifies topology only and says nothing about energy, geometry, affinity, kinetics, or yield.
costs: The algorithm takes G and f as supplied; identifying sites, target degrees, candidate edges, and edge legality must be charged upstream.
Naive all-pairs candidate-edge generation may require Theta(n^2) tests and may dominate the solver.
Repeated independent runs can reduce false-negative probability to at most 3^(-r) at r times the run cost; this is an elementary amplification deduction, not a release guarantee.
claims.falsifier: A target system whose legal choices require weights, parallel bond types, geometric coupling, or non-degree constraints without a sound explicit encoding makes this interface inapplicable to that system; this does not refute the graph theorem.
claims.next_gate: For a named chemical system, define data acquisition and legality precisely, then prove that the full decision predicate is preserved by the simple-graph exact-degree encoding.

claims.exact_statement: In the explicit toy model with two rigid bivalent scaffolds, four inter-scaffold sites at square corners, G=K_2,2, f(v)=2 for all four vertices, LJ cross-contact potential U_LJ(r)=4 epsilon[(sigma/r)^12-(sigma/r)^6], side r0=2^(1/6)sigma, and per-site angle penalty U_theta=0.5 k_theta(theta-pi)^2 with k_theta=16 epsilon/pi^2, the unique f-factor is geometrically realized but has association energy change Delta U=8 epsilon-4 epsilon=4 epsilon>0 relative to separated scaffolds. For epsilon=1 kcal/mol, T=298 K, and the stated toy assumption Delta G standard=Delta U, Ka*c_standard=exp(-4/(RT)) approximately 1.17e-3; at equal 1 micromolar concentrations the dilute bound fraction is approximately 1.2e-9.
assumptions: The square is rigid, so the 90-degree contact angles cannot relax.
Each of the four inter-scaffold contacts contributes its LJ minimum -epsilon; the four angle penalties are active only in the assembled state.
For the illustrative equilibrium calculation only, standard free energy equals the specified energy change, with no additional entropy, solvent, or reference-state contribution.
claims.status: INTERNALLY RECONSTRUCTED COUNTEREXAMPLE IN A DEFINED TOY ENERGY MODEL; not a measured molecular system or empirical yield prediction.
claims.proof_path: work/agents/reaction_recognition_logic/FINAL_REPORT.md#explicit-energetic-counterexample; numerical RT and equilibrium exponent checked with the local Python math library.
claims.novelty_boundary: The counterexample establishes only that graph feasibility alone implies no favorable energy or binding guarantee. Force-field papers support the relevance of pair and angular energy terms, not the toy parameter values or a claim about a real molecule.
costs: Hand calculation: four contacts at -epsilon; four harmonic angle penalties at +2 epsilon each; net +4 epsilon.
RT at 298 K is approximately 0.5922 kcal/mol; exp(-4/RT) is approximately 0.0011655.
No force-field fitting, conformational search, solvent calculation, standard-state correction beyond the stated toy assumption, or experimental measurement was performed.
claims.falsifier: An arithmetic error in the specified potential and geometry, or failure of the expressly stated toy equilibrium assumptions, would invalidate the numerical illustration. It does not challenge the matching theorem.
claims.next_gate: If an empirical claim is wanted, choose a real pair of scaffolds, fit or select an explicit physical model, optimize/measure the bound ensemble and free energy, and compare topology-only prediction against those data.

claims.exact_statement: Prescribed-degree factors are classical polynomial-time graph objects: Anstee (1985) reports an O(n^3)-operation algorithm returning an f-factor or establishing nonexistence. Molecular graph enumeration literature predates family 120 and includes constructive enumeration with prescribed valence states and empirical formula, and later colored-multigraph/edge-multiplicity constraints. Therefore the application route is not a new chemical feasibility predicate; its potential algorithmic contribution is the source-reported faster graph-level algorithm on the narrower simple f-factor interface.
assumptions: Prior-art abstracts and bibliographic records accurately represent the cited primary works.
Comparisons are asymptotic and problem-level; word-RAM conventions, determinism, error, output and implementation costs differ.
claims.status: PRIMARY-ART COMPARISON; citations checked, no full comparative implementation benchmark.
claims.novelty_boundary: No claim of exhaustive prior-art coverage or priority is made. The source theorem is not independently validated here.
costs: Anstee's cited abstract reports O(n^3) operations; it is not benchmarked against the family-120 word-RAM implementation.
Chemical graph enumeration may output exponentially many structures; no output-sensitive complexity comparison was reconstructed.
claims.falsifier: A materially different statement in the primary cited works would require revising this limited comparison.
claims.next_gate: Read full primary papers and compare formal graph models and input/output costs before making a stronger novelty or dominance claim.
